source.title: From Colors to Classes: Emergence of Concepts in Vision Transformers
source.authors: Teresa Dorszewski; Lenka Tetková; Robert Jenssen; Lars Kai Hansen; Kristoffer Wickstrøm

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how many vision-model neurons receive labels above a similarity threshold, which bears conceptually on V4's claim about the share of interpretable neurons. It does not compare explanation tools or test the proposed causes of interpretability.
record.gate_note: The paper assigns each neuron one CLIP-Dissect label, then reports counts above an adaptive threshold. These counts bear on V4 as a threshold-dependent proxy for labeled neurons, but do not establish that each neuron has one job: labels are selected from a fixed concept list, and explanations are not tested on held-out activations. The layer-wise category and image-complexity results do not measure the claim versions' named outcomes. Cited prior studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses CLIP-Dissect neuron labels to map which concepts ViT layers encode. It assumes some monosemanticity and never measures the share of interpretable neurons. Its labeled-neuron counts come from thresholding at each layer's mean similarity score, so they are fixed by that choice (about 40% of neurons) and are not a measured share. It compares no explanation tools and tests no causes, so it bears on no version, V4 included.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that ViTs, despite global attention, encode concepts hierarchically like CNNs: colors and textures early, objects and organisms late, with more distinct concepts in later layers. Pretraining strategy shapes concept categories. Finetuning reduces the number of concepts and shifts them toward task-relevant categories, most strongly for out-of-distribution data. They acknowledge mean-thresholding suppresses differences in interpretable-neuron counts between layers and models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CLIP-Dissect neuron labeling on vision transformers and ResNet50, not the language-model neuron audit or tested explanation-prediction procedure described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The count of labeled neurons depends on the similarity-score threshold: the authors use a separate mean threshold per layer, and state that a fixed threshold would make DINOv2 stand out with more labeled neurons. They also note that the adaptive threshold suppresses differences among layers and models.

fits_no_version.finding: Neurons in four ViTs and ResNet50 shift from colors and textures in early layers to objects and organisms in late layers. The number of distinct concepts roughly doubles across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-neuron labels in ViTs show a hierarchy of concept complexity similar to CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: DINOv2 neuron descriptions have higher CLIP-Dissect similarity scores (mean threshold about 0.21 versus about 0.17). The authors read this as possibly more monosemantic neurons, but give no share.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training objective (self-distillation) may raise how well neurons fit single labels.

record.peer_reviewed: The 3rd World Conference on eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (accepted)
record.problems: The labeled-neuron counts depend on an adaptive threshold that the authors say suppresses between-model and between-layer differences. Concept categories were partly assigned using language models and manual judgment, and the paper does not test labels against held-out activations.

untested.parts: All. The study is not on Qwen3-32B, does no pole audit and measures no job shares.
All. It covers vision models only, with no language models and no scaling.
All. It does not examine InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or pose features.
All. It makes no tool comparison, no architecture or regularization cause test, and measures no interpretable share (counts are fixed by thresholding).
All. It builds no attribution graphs.
All. It does not test labels on held-out activations.
All. It does no simulation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 limits_scope label is dropped. The counts are selection values from thresholding at each layer's mean, so they cannot show the interpretable share rising or falling. The 55-80% fitting and 20-30% uninterpretable figures come from the cited CLIP-Dissect user study, not from this study, so they are not rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure positive and negative neuron poles, one-versus-two jobs, or the share not understood; its single-label assignment is not a test of those properties.
Studies vision models, not language models or dense/MoE language-model scaling.
Does not examine InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test recursive generalization versus superposition.

Does not compare explanation tools, establish architecture or regularization as causes, compare model capacity, or test the cited InceptionV1-sized estimates. Its adaptive threshold prevents a straightforward comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across models.
Does not build attribution graphs or test whether a model's own neurons suffice as circuit units.
Does not test whether explanations derived from activating examples predict firing on new examples.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text or report such scores.

rows.subject: ViT (sup-ViT)
rows.operation_detail: Counted neurons whose CLIP-Dissect similarity score exceeded the layer's mean threshold; table reports averages across layers for ViT models.
rows.measure: Number of labeled neurons above threshold
rows.note: The table calls the model ViT; the text describes the supervised model as sup-ViT. The adaptive threshold was chosen to produce comparable numbers of labeled neurons, so this count does not directly establish an interpretable-neuron share.
rows.check: Selection value. The count of neurons above the per-layer mean threshold is set by the thresholding rule, so it is not a measured interpretable share. It bears on no version.

rows.subject: DINOv2
rows.operation_detail: Counted neurons whose CLIP-Dissect similarity score exceeded the layer's mean threshold; table reports averages across layers for ViT models.
rows.measure: Number of labeled neurons above threshold
rows.note: The authors state that a fixed threshold would yield a higher number of labeled neurons for DINOv2; mean-thresholding suppresses differences in label counts across models.
rows.check: Selection value set by mean thresholding. The authors say only that a fixed threshold would give DINOv2 more concepts, with no number.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Counts obtained using the paper's per-layer mean similarity threshold
reader_labels.reason: The paper says this thresholding makes labeled-neuron counts comparable by design and suppresses differences between layers and models; a fixed threshold would give DINOv2 more labeled neurons (r1–r9). These results do not establish the claimed rise in interpretable share across architectures or tools.
